supersedes: modern/spec/pic2d/pic2d-foundation-v1.json (equations, gates and artifact contracts unchanged; this file records the v1.1 additions)

time_step_v1_1.all_gpu_step: deposit -> device block-Thomas field solve -> gather/push (electrons every step, ions every k steps) -> boundaries -> MCC -> injection -> compaction/spawn all on the device; the host reads a small statistics vector and the particle counts every device_sync_steps steps only

poisson.method: device-direct (PoissonConfig2D.method = 'device-direct'): the block-Thomas factorisation of the reduced cylindrical Gauss matrix is built once on the host and copied to the device; each step runs the forward/backward sweeps as one kernel launch per radial block with 256-lane coalesced row dot products and deterministic tile reductions
poisson.tolerance_contract: the true residual ||A phi - b|| <= relative_tolerance * ||b|| (1e-10 in the v2 protocol) is recomputed on the device and checked at every host sync; a violation raises PIC2DStabilityError (fail closed)
poisson.parity: phi equals the host direct solve to 1e-10 relative on the first step; electron positions agree to 1e-15 m after the first push (tests/pic2d/test_pic2d_v11_step.py)
poisson.pcg_status: device Jacobi-PCG with warm start from the previous phi remains available (method = 'pcg'); on these grids the direct device solve is faster than the 500-1000 PCG iterations per step, so it is the default for the GPU backend and PCG is kept as a cross-check

time_step_v1_1.kernel_reductions: per-particle same-address float64 atomics for the work, speed^2 and the five collision tallies were replaced by per-block wp.tile_sum / wp.tile_max reductions (block 256) followed by one atomic per block; the absorbed counts are exact integers identical to the numpy reference, the work sum agrees to 1e-9 of the gross kinetic energy

ion_subcycling.rule: ions are pushed every k steps with k dt; ionisation-born ions are added to the ion charge immediately and receive their first push at the next ion step; the ion velocity is staggered by k dt / 2 (leapfrog)
ion_subcycling.budget: k dt = 12 ps at dt = 1.5 ps; ion plasma period at n_max = 4e17 m^-3 is 2 pi / omega_pi = 90 ns (omega_pi k dt = 8.8e-4); ion cyclotron period at 0.29 T is 29 us; a 21 km/s ion (300 V) moves 0.25 um per ion step (< 1 % of a fine cell)
ion_subcycling.insensitivity: k = 4 vs k = 8 over 400 steps: identical ion count, mean ion position within 1e-6 of the domain, mean phi within 1e-3, ion kinetic energy within 2.5 % (the half-step stagger of a cold population accelerating from rest)

electrode_work.relation: for each Dirichlet electrode k at V_k the supply provides dQ_src = dQ_induced,k - q_absorbed,k per interval, with Q_induced,k = sum over the electrode's Dirichlet nodes of (A phi)_k (the conductor charge of the discrete Gauss law) and q_absorbed the net charge of particles absorbed there; the ledger source term gains sum_k V_k dQ_src,k
electrode_work.verification: with the term the cumulative residual of a 300 V discharge is <= 15 % of both the total-energy change and the electrode work, and the electrode work exceeds half the total-energy change (it is the dominant budget term); without it the ledger misses the whole supply work

operating_point_v1_1.why: v1 ran at n_g = 5e20 m^-3 and 100 mA: the ionisation source exceeded the unmagnetised Bohm ion loss 12x at the observed T_e = 18 eV, so the density had to grow until ions reach the walls (~1 us); it hit the omega_pe dt gate at 49-60 ns. At n_g = 1e20 the particle balance closes at T_e = 7.9 eV (amplification 2.4 at 18 eV) and a 0-D power balance gives n_eq ~ 2e17 m^-3; the design ceiling for the numerics budget is n_max = 4e17 m^-3 (2x margin)
operating_point_v1_1.zero_d_estimate: n_g <sigma_iz v>(T_e) n_e V = n_e v_Bohm(T_e) A_loss with V = 3.5e-7 m^3 and A_loss = 3.6e-4 m^2 (walls + exit + anode; unmagnetised Bohm loss is an upper bound on the loss, so n_eq is a lower bound); power balance 300 V * I_d = n_eq v_Bohm A_loss (E_iz + 2 T_e + wall sheath losses)

coarse.note: deliberately under-resolved member of the convergence pair

particles_per_cell_at_n_max.note: electrons per cell in the annulus at r = 1 mm (fine V_cell = 2 pi r dr dz = 1.05e-11 m^3, coarse 4x); at the expected mean density 1e17 divide by 4

resolution_budget_v1_1.dt_lesson: a first v2 attempt at dt = 3 ps was stopped fail-closed after 0.27 us in both coarse cases: the runtime gate evaluates the instantaneous peak node density, and the axis nodes (a handful of macro-particles) carry ~3x shot noise on top of the window-averaged peak (1.4e18 instantaneous vs 4.7-5.4e17 window peak). Halving dt moves the trip density to 5.6e18 m^-3, 14x the design ceiling, so the gate again only fires on a genuine runaway

performance.before_v1_1: v1 fine case (60 x 480, 5.4 M macro-particles): 40.7 ms/step; host block-Thomas solve 18 ms/step plus per-step host<->device particle-count and statistics copies
performance.after_v1_1: same fine case with device-direct Poisson, ion subcycling k = 8 and tile-reduced kernels: 5.46 ms/step (Poisson 2.3 ms/step) = 1.0 ns per particle-step; coarse v2 cases (0.13-0.27 M particles) run at 1.2-2.0 ms/step with four cases sharing the GPU
performance.single_process_from_v2_checkpoints: 2.04 ms/step at 1.53 M macro-particles (30 x 240), 4.34 ms/step at 3.8 M and 5.45 ms/step at 5.3 M (60 x 480): 1.0-1.3 ns per particle-step above a ~1.2 ms launch-bound floor
performance.target: <= 1.5 ms/step at 1-2 M macro-particles was not met (2.0 ms at 1.5 M); the remaining cost is ~40 kernel launches per step on a WDDM host, removable only by CUDA-graph capture of the full step (blocked by the dynamic particle bounds) or by a TCC/Linux host
performance.launch_overhead_note: kernel launches on this WDDM host cost ~0.5 ms each when the GPU is shared; the step is launch-bound below ~1 M particles, which is why the kernels were fused/reduced rather than further vectorised

tests: tests/pic2d/test_pic2d_v11_step.py: device-direct parity and residual contract; tile-reduced tallies exact; subcycling k vs 2k; ledger closes with electrode work; ion_subcycle provenance
tests/pic2d/test_pic2d_warp_parity.py: CPU/GPU parity of deposition (bitwise), push, MCC statistics, PCG vs direct still green
unchanged_simplifications: static uniform neutral background (no depletion: the 0-D ionisation rate ~2e17 s^-1 removes ~1 % of the 3.4e13 channel neutrals over 1.6 us at n_g = 1e20 m^-3, locally a few per cent; deferred and stated, documented in pic2d-formulation.md)
no ion-neutral elastic or charge-exchange collisions (deferred: the Biagi Xe+-Xe set is not in the hash-bound extract)
no secondary emission; Dirichlet exit plane; prescribed B; electrostatic; momentum-conserving scheme
